messages:
anika: starting canary for marble11b (int4) today. hitting intermittent cuda OOMs on dense-qa when prefetch is enabled. looping in infra + eng-ml.

ron: is this on dedicated canary pool or hosted infra? what instance type?

anika: dedicated canary pool (p4d-2021 equivalent). failure rate ~1 in 8 requests. stack points to allocation failing inside KV prefetch path: 
```
ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
kv_prefetch: queued=52, reserve_attempt=140MB, alloc_failed_at=512MB
trace: slot_compactor invoked, free_slots=10, reserved=48MB
```

lucas: okay. what's the rollout config? prefetch + batch sizing + max_new_tokens can blow up transient allocs.

anika: rollout values: batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=160, prefetch=true, kv_hot_threshold=0.65

mai: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) drop default max_new_tokens to 64 for the model on canary; 2) switch prefetch heuristic to `kv_trim` (evict cold keys during scan) instead of full eager prefetch; both should cut peak allocations. command: `redwoodctl config set marble11b --default.max_new_tokens=64`

lucas: also try lowering batch_size to 1 for the canary pool to determine if aggregate per-request allocations are cumulative. If OOMs stop, it's a batching pressure issue.

anika: applying changes: set max_new_tokens=64 and batch_size=1 on canary, leaving prefetch=true for now to measure tail impact.

dev-bot: [alert] canary marble11b v0.3.1 failure-rate=3.8%. rollout controller rolled back to v0.3.0 at 6567901200 due to elevated failures.

anika: saw rollback trigger. post-rollback logs still show 1 spike per ~600 requests. allocator profile suggests slab fragmentation plus delayed compaction.

ron: can you capture heap stats at spike time? `redwoodctl debug heap-stats --model marble11b --node <node-id>` should help.

anika: pasted sanitized heap stats: 
```
heap_total: 24GB
skipped_free_chunks: 9
slab_sizes: {64MB: 110, 128MB: 52, 256MB: 14}
freelist_count: 7
avg_alloc_latency_ms: 2.1
compaction_runs_last_min: 0
fragmentation_ratio: 0.76
```

mai: compaction_runs_last_min=0 and frag_ratio=0.76 — compactor threshold default is 0.8 so it didn't run. two safe knobs: lower frag_threshold to 0.7 for this pool, and enable `allocator.defrag_before_prefetch=true` to do a quick micro-defrag before heavy prefetch.

lucas: agreed. additional option: enable `kv_walk`/`kv_trim` heuristic to avoid loading long tail keys. That reduces peak working set.

anika: making changes: `redwoodctl feature set --pool canary-marble --allocator.frag_threshold=0.7` and `redwoodctl config set marble11b --allocator.defrag_before_prefetch=true --prefetch.heuristic=kv_trim`

anika: after changes ran 12k requests, zero OOMs, p95 latency increased by ~20ms with micro-defrag + kv_trim. tail seems improved, throughput steady.

ron: nice. we should add an automated rollback guard: if failure_rate > 1% OR p95_latency_delta > 25ms sustained for 5m, flip prefetch off for that model/pool to limit blast radius.

mai: added rollout guard policy: 
```
policy {
  trigger: failure_rate > 0.01 OR p95_latency_delta > 25ms FOR 5m
  action: set model.config.prefetch=false
}
```

anika: policy attached to canary-marble. proposing new onboarding defaults for marble11b: batch_size=1, max_new_tokens=64, allocator.frag_threshold=0.7, allocator.defrag_before_prefetch=true, prefetch.heuristic=kv_trim.

lucas: let's also run the nightly eval to compare QA metrics with reduced max_new_tokens. schedule and compare EM/F1.

anika: eval job queued (eval-6567901255). initial quick diff shows EM delta within noise (-0.15% EM). will post full eval report once complete. thanks team :rocket:

mai: great triage — thanks! :thumbsup:

dev-bot: [info] eval job queued: eval-id=eval-6567901255
